findings.issue: `.cmd` shims are resolved safely, but the command processor is taken from `process.env.ComSpec` without any realpath, repo/temp, or approved-root validation.
findings.exploit: On Windows, set `ComSpec` to an attacker-controlled executable or `.cmd`, then dispatch any allowed `.cmd`-backed tool such as `safeSpawnSync("claude", allowedArgs)`. `resolveTool()` may return the legitimate `claude.cmd`, but `safeSpawnSync()` executes the attacker-controlled `ComSpec` first with `/c`.
findings.fix: Do not trust `ComSpec`. Use a canonical realpathed `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe` and verify it is outside repo/temp and under an approved Windows system root, or validate `ComSpec` with the same resolver before use.

findings.issue: `treeKill()` bypasses the safety kernel by spawning unqualified `taskkill` directly.
findings.exploit: Plant `taskkill.cmd`/`taskkill.exe` earlier in PATH or in the process search path, then cause any allowed child command to time out. The timeout path invokes `spawnSync("taskkill", ...)`, executing the planted binary despite the `resolveTool('taskkill')` policy existing elsewhere.
findings.fix: Resolve `taskkill` to an absolute, validated path once, preferably `%SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe`, and spawn only that path. Do not use PATH lookup in the kill path.

findings.issue: `assertArgs()` does not reject Windows cmd variable-expansion metacharacters `%` and `!`, even though accepted args are later passed through `cmd.exe /c` for `.cmd` shims.
findings.exploit: Set an environment variable such as `EVIL=& calc & rem`, then pass an otherwise valid consumed value like `PROJECT_ROOT + "\\%EVIL%"` to `codex -o`. I verified `assertArgs('codex', ['exec','-o', PROJECT_ROOT + '\\%EVIL%', '-'])` returns `ok:true`. When routed through `cmd.exe /c`, `%EVIL%` expands before the shim runs and turns into a command separator payload.
findings.fix: For any `.cmd` shim invocation, reject `%` and `!` in every argument and in the shim path, or avoid `cmd.exe` entirely where possible. Also run with a scrubbed environment containing no attacker-controlled expansion variables.

findings.issue: The approved-root guard is optional, so default resolution still accepts PATH hijacks outside the repo and OS temp directory.
findings.exploit: With no `WARPOS_APPROVED_TOOL_ROOTS` set, a planted `claude.cmd` in a user-writable PATH directory such as `%APPDATA%\npm` or Downloads passes because it is neither repo-local nor under `os.tmpdir()`. `which()` returns the first PATH hit and `resolveTool()` accepts it by default.
findings.fix: Make approved tool roots mandatory for dispatch, validate them with realpath boundary checks, and reject user-writable roots. Alternatively pin each tool to an explicit installed path instead of accepting arbitrary PATH hits.

findings.issue: The `git` policy allows broad `git config` positionals, which gives the model Git-level code execution/persistence primitives despite no shell metacharacters.
findings.exploit: I verified `assertArgs('git', ['config','alias.pwn','!calc'])` returns `ok:true`. That writes a Git alias whose later invocation executes `calc` via Git's shell alias mechanism. Similar broad config writes can alter hooks, includes, or SSH command behavior.
findings.fix: Remove `git config` from the generic allowlist, or restrict it to exact read-only forms such as `git config --get <known-safe-key>`. Explicitly reject `alias.*`, `core.hooksPath`, `core.sshCommand`, `include.*`, and values beginning with `!`.

findings.issue: `cwd_policy: "worktree-required"` is only checked if `req.cwd` is supplied, so callers can omit `cwd` and still pass validation.
findings.exploit: For the canonical registry, `validateDispatch({role:'frontend-builder', shape:'subprocess-claude', toolId:'claude'})` returns `ok:true` even though the resolved contract requires an isolated worktree. A downstream dispatcher can then fall back to the canonical project root and violate the build-chain isolation invariant.
findings.fix: If `cwd_policy === "worktree-required"`, require `req.cwd` to be present. Resolve realpaths and verify it is not the canonical root and is under an expected worktree root.

findings.issue: The hard build-chain/in-process invariant depends on env-overridable registry identity.
findings.exploit: Set `WARPOS_ROLE_REGISTRY_PATH` before module load to a crafted registry where `frontend-builder` has `build_chain:false` and a class that allows `in-process-agent`. The hard check at lines 136-139 reads that overridden registry, so the canonical build-chain role can be made to validate as in-process.
findings.fix: Do not honor registry/contract path overrides in runtime dispatch, or gate them to tests only. For production, pin the canonical registry path by realpath and make the hard invariant derive from that trusted file.

parsed.summary: Dotenv parsing itself is in-code and I did not find a path where `dotenvParse()` executes shell syntax or the CLI report prints secret values. The ordinary canonical `build_chain && shape === 'in-process-agent'` check is present. The module set still fails because Windows command-processor trust, unqualified `taskkill`, optional approved roots, cmd variable expansion, broad Git config, and env-overridable registry identity leave exploitable dispatch-safety bypasses.
